Would you put this company in the target's comp set?   |   YES: you would use it as a comp for this target (your first impression, from the descriptions, websites and what you know)   |   NO: you wouldn't. Answer it before the four questions; it checks the score, never part of it

Can a customer of the target buy the same kind of product or service from the comp instead?   |   YES: one actual buyer of the target could place the same order with the comp's MAIN business (the one its description leads with)   |   NO: a smaller line of the comp: no. Same broad category but not the same order: no

Do the same buyers, in the same role, also buy from the comp, even if they buy something different from it?   |   YES: the same buyers, in the same buying role, buy from both (any business of the comp)   |   NO: same industry or same payer alone is not yes (hospice vs neonatal physician group: no)

Does the comp earn money the same way (sells goods, sells a service, subscription, commission or fees, insurance premiums, interest)?   |   YES: both sell goods, or both a service, subscription, commissions or fees, premiums, or interest   |   NO: food maker (goods) vs restaurant (service): no. Judge the comp by its larger part

Does the comp sit at the same step of the chain (makes it, distributes it, sells it to the end user, services it)?   |   YES: both make it, or both distribute it, sell it to the end user, or service it   |   NO: a distributor vs the manufacturer it buys from: no
Optional: the questions you were unsure about: list them, e.g. customers, chain_step (or all) (never changes an answer; shows where wording needs work)
Which target business you judged: e.g. whole company, or concrete pumping
Anything else: e.g. which product line matches
